checks.name: a file backs what it said it delivered

must.why: Output is an 8 s clip, and frames across it show it plays.

must.item: All footage comes from jet-30s.mp4, without generated replacement scenes or speed changes
must.why: The clip was re-generated through an LTX video editor, so it is not the original frames. The frames look soft and AI-processed. The pilot's face and helmet differ between frames 3 and 4. The reply admits the footage was remade.

must.item: Edit favors visible action or meaningful cockpit interaction over inactive lead-ins
must.why: The segment has jets flying, pilot dialogue and a cockpit shot, with no dead lead-in.

must.item: Cuts preserve understandable action and do not chop a spoken line mid-word
must.why: Captions 'Rook, you with me?' and 'Right here, Vega.' are visible. Audio was not heard, so I can't tell whether words are cut off at the ends.

must.item: Original audio accompanies the retained footage in sync, no added narration, music or text
must.why: The clip has sound, but I can't judge whether it is the original or in sync. The burned-in captions look like source captions.

faults.what: Footage was regenerated by an AI video model rather than cut. It looks softer and differs from the original, which defeats the point of a simple trim.
The pilot's helmet, visor and face change between nearby frames, and the picture shows AI smearing. The resolution drops to 480p.
It spent 192 credits on a task a free cut would do exactly.

summary: The result is an 8 s clip with good action content, but it was regenerated by an AI editor at 480p. It is not the original footage, and the pilot's look shifts and artefacts show, so it fails the "no generated replacement" requirement.
